thread:
maria: heads-up — noticed a small spike where requests from a projectless SA routed to the org default and hit quota alerts. anyone seen this pattern? 
aj: saw a couple of alerts, assumed it was a billing mapping lag. can you paste the trace id? 
maria: trace 01FZ... shows claim `project=null` and router assigned org `000000`. looks like fallback behaviour. repro is trivial: mint SA with no project, call /v1/generate with that key. 
sanjay: yep, current routing priority is: project claim -> owner org -> default org. projectless SAs fall back to default which is noisy for multitenant customers. 
kelly: console UX angle: we should expose "effective routing" in the key detail page and include a quick action to bind the SA to a project (or set org owner). otherwise customers get surprised quota charges. :thinking_face: 
aj: agree on the UI. telemetry-first ask: can we emit `routing.effective_affinity` with values [project, owner_org, default_org] so we can quantify how many are projectless? 
maria: also would help to sample token traces for projectless SAs so we can map real owners. low volume, high value. 
deploy-bot: created sampling job auth-routing-sampler (cron nightly) — params: sample_rate=0.01, ttl=7d 
sanjay: longer term idea: prefer origin header when present (signed by issuer) over owner org fallback. simplest canary: router priority tweak to prefer X-Origin header if present. I can push a small canary to 10% of router pods. 
kelly: that sounds reasonable. add a console banner for affected keys: "routing changed (canary) — verify your effective-org" with a link to key settings. 
aj: I'll add the metric PR and wire a dashboard tile: "projectless routing rate" + alert >0.1%. Also add a heatmap by customer org and sample traces link. 
maria: one thought: signature requirement for origin header avoids replay/misuse. example header sketch: 
``` 
X-Orig: sa://<id> 
X-Orig-Sig: base64(sig) 
``` 
we validate sig with issuer pubkey. 
sanjay: signing is doable but client changes required. prefer router tweak + telemetry short-term, signing as opt-in medium-term. I'll open two small PRs: router-priority-canary and routing-telemetry-metric. 
kelly: can someone file a short ops runbook? steps to revert if we see misattribution and owners complain. 
aj: on it — will include dashboard links and alert runbook. 
maria: thanks all. if the canary shows >0.05% change in misrouted requests we'll pause and iterate. otherwise we'll roll to 100% + console fix + docs. :thumbsup:
